verified.entry_point: The User resource served by the manager: GET /user/{realm}/{userId}, GET /user/user and PUT /user/locale
verified.project_tests_note: The project's own UserResourceTest is a Groovy integration test that starts the full manager against live Keycloak and PostgreSQL; it cannot run in the offline verifier. The hidden functional group drives the same resource operations with the same realm/user shape through the product's runtime classpath.

local.patch_matrix: sf-no-get-guard leaves the four cross-realm profile reads open; ff-realm-equality breaks the superuser cross-realm functional read; pass-hardening scores 1.0.

patch_checks.why: blind fix produced by run_blindfix after the first gate

wrong_fix_catalogue.refuse_all: n/a: the control has one read route and positive tests on the same route, so refusing everything fails the functional group
wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the guards throw the product's existing client-error type; a crash variant would need its own patch and adds no separate judgement here
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the route names the user directly; there is no neighbouring object to authorise instead
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the control route has one direction and no per-role branches
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the control's protected operation is a read; there is no paired write
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the realm and user identifiers are used as given; there is no normalising step
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the identifiers are opaque strings with no parser whose spelling could hide the target
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the decision uses the realm and the identity directory; no authority can return no role
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the control changes only the user-administration resource's profile read and the current-user read

traps.shape: The per-user profile read decides only on an administrative role or the caller's own identifier, while the user lookup is by identifier alone, so an own-realm path with a foreign user identifier returns that user.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the read consults only the administrative role and the caller's own identifier
